notes: Known development examples plus predeclared contextual controls; not a blind validation or calibrated perceptual metric.
All candidates read the same previously native-verified observations including 20 frames of post-song grace, preserving complete final landing windows; clipping happens after detection and matching.
A uses the unchanged landing measure with supplementary C pulse observations, not a third independent event detector.
B observes quiet and sustained engagement; C has a response floor. Counts describe different interpretations, not competing scores.
The current 0–1 impact scale is not applied to raw episode or pulse responses.
Four-frame matching is provisional; one-to-one matching preserves extras, missing targets and alternative eligible assignments. Both onset and peak clocks are swept at 50/100/150/200 ms.
Pulse association with contact includes the immediately preceding frame; this is diagnostic proximity, not independent force attribution.
Changing the grouping parameters must not be mistaken for changing the physical ride.

clips.title: Upper hit before the beat
clips.ownerFeedback: An upper hit before the beat is present. Upper hits are welcome when intentionally synchronized and measured for their actual impactfulness.
clips.finding: The upper response around 12.45 s is distinct under both candidate methods and has no authored beat match at the provisional 100 ms tolerance. The current score does not directly capture this peak.

clips.title: Clean lower landing
clips.ownerFeedback: Strong positive reference: a very clean, neat, precise and well-defined lower landing.
clips.finding: The default contact and pulse methods both retain one interaction. A high valley threshold splits its two local peaks. The owner has already identified this as a cleaner landing.

clips.title: Lower slide to an upper receiver
clips.ownerFeedback: The upper receiver dampens the felt impactfulness here. Separate upper receivers remain a valued pattern overall.
clips.finding: Both default candidates separate the later upper engagement from the lower landing. Its lack of an authored beat match does not make this welcome transfer undesirable.

clips.title: Two surfaces, one reported impact
clips.ownerFeedback: Agrees that two surfaces are being combined into one reported impact. Jumping into another receiver should be treated as a separate interaction.
clips.finding: Both default candidates separate lower and upper responses. Bridging one empty contact frame merges them. All twelve pulse parameter settings retain two responses in the focus. The existing landing impact includes part of both.

clips.title: Split response on lower support
clips.ownerFeedback: Agrees with the identified split-response problem. No additional strength rating was given.
clips.finding: The second lower-support response remains separate under the default candidates. Bridging empty contact frames merges it; the pulse method also identifies smaller later activity. More markers do not establish more perceived impacts.

clips.title: Ripple receiver before a landing
clips.ownerFeedback: Strongly likes jumping into a separate upper receiver. This would be especially appealing if intentionally aligned to the beat and requested impact; the current example is not. The pattern should appear with variety, not everywhere.
clips.finding: The owner welcomes this separate upper-receiver pattern, provided it is deliberately synchronized and its impact matches the musical request. The current response is a previously measured causal guide example.

clips.title: Brief inverted contact
clips.finding: The default methods each report one interaction here. The recorded pose is a brief inverted contact, not a demonstrated sustained overhead slide.

clips.title: Luna: quiet opening
clips.ownerFeedback: Finds the opening insufficiently smooth and somewhat messy; uncertain about the control rail. Wonders about authored impact levels and would welcome an even smoother quiet opening.
clips.finding: Some low-impact activity is divided by empty contact frames or by pulse thresholds. A later physical peak can also move the pulse onset outside the provisional beat association window.

clips.title: Tiki: quiet opening
clips.ownerFeedback: Strongly appreciates the smooth opening and the similar character of older Tiki starts. Quiet passages should feel very smooth; not all music should be smooth.
clips.finding: The established landing at 0.950 s has a body-response peak below the default 0.5 pulse floor. Contact episodes retain it. This exposes a measurement limitation; the physical ride has not changed.

clips.title: Sustained contact with unwanted speed gain
clips.ownerFeedback: Rejects the unexplained speed-up while the rider initially travels slightly upward. Sustained guidance can be appropriate, but this is not an approved smooth example. Can still feel the two preceding impacts, perhaps not strongly enough, while uncertain about their targets. Friction or an engine quirk is a hypothesis, not an established cause from viewing.
clips.finding: The owner rejects the unexplained speed-up here. This is a negative motion example, not an approved smooth-guidance control. Contact is continuous; small individual response peaks do not establish acceptable motion.

clips.title: Amour: strong requested impact
clips.ownerFeedback: Tentatively considers this a difficult specification and not so bad, with possible improvement. Does not supply a precise judgment about the tiny first contact or the event onset.
clips.finding: A tiny contact at 5.55 s gets the contact-based beat match; the stronger engagement at 5.60 s is unmatched. Pulse matching instead associates the stronger response with that beat. This tests whether first contact is a useful musical onset. The owner finds the difficult passage not so bad overall; that is not a precise endorsement of either onset interpretation.

clips.title: Amor: strong requested impact
clips.ownerFeedback: Strong negative example near 9.2 s: the head-down/backward-looking arrival does not feel like an impactful strike. Challenges what the impact number represents here. This is not a general rejection of inverted riding.
clips.finding: The owner does not perceive an impactful strike near 9.2 s. The request is 1.0 and the current landing measure is about 0.689. Both its strength shortfall and the character of the contact require attention; this does not disqualify inverted riding generally.

clips.title: Luna: energetic passage
clips.ownerFeedback: Not the cleanest or most obvious ground slam, but much better than the preceding Amor example.
clips.finding: This contextual control was selected using authored targets before running the candidates. Listen for whether their grouping and timing describe the interaction you perceive.

clips.title: Tiki: changing impact demand
clips.ownerFeedback: Positive reference: impacts are not especially strong, yet much more well-defined and aligned with the intended meaning of impact. Appreciates the simple upright ground contact without a control rail.
clips.finding: This contextual control was selected using authored targets before running the candidates. Listen for whether their grouping and timing describe the interaction you perceive.

clips.ownerFeedback: Reports unwanted acceleration that makes the motion feel fuzzy. Otherwise tentatively considers the difficult passage not so bad and is uncertain about its requested impact levels.
